### ecr-repository-policy-default-account-only

**Write it as.** `only the AWS account that created the repository` · `a repository policy that allows additional access`

**Scope.** Amazon ECR repositories; default; adjustable.

> "By default, only the AWS account that created the repository has access to the repository. You can apply a repository policy that allows additional access to your repository."
> — [Private repository policies in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/repository-policies.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### ecr-repository-policy-vs-iam-policy-evaluation

**Claim.** ECR repository policies are a subset of IAM policies scoped to individual repositories; if an action is allowed by one policy type but denied by the other, the action is denied, and a user or role needs permission for an action through only one of them for the action to be allowed. However, Amazon ECR requires that users have permission to call the ecr:GetAuthorizationToken API through an IAM policy before they can authenticate to a registry and push or pull any images.

**Write it as.** `repository policies are a subset of IAM policies` · `the action will be denied` · `either a repository policy or an IAM policy`

**Scope.** Amazon ECR repository access.

> "Amazon ECR repository policies are a subset of IAM policies that are scoped for, and specifically used for, controlling access to individual Amazon ECR repositories."
> — [Private repository policies in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/repository-policies.html)

> "If a user or role is allowed to perform an action through a repository policy but is denied permission through an IAM policy (or vice versa) then the action will be denied. A user or role only needs to be allowed permission for an action through either a repository policy or an IAM policy but not both for the action to be allowed."
> — [Private repository policies in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/repository-policies.html)

> "Amazon ECR requires that users have permission to make calls to the `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken` API through an IAM policy before they can authenticate to a registry and push or pull any images from any Amazon ECR repository."
> — [Private repository policies in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/repository-policies.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### ecr-rules-per-lifecycle-policy-limit

**Claim.** An ECR lifecycle policy can have at most 50 rules. The quota is not adjustable.

**Write it as.** `50 rules`

**Scope.** per lifecycle policy, per Region; maximum; not adjustable.

> "Rules per lifecycle policy | Each supported Region: 50 | No | The maximum number of rules in a lifecycle policy" (columns: Name | Default | Adjustable | Description)
> — [Amazon ECR service quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/service-quotas.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### ecr-scan-on-push-each-new-image

**Claim.** Each ECR repository can be configured to scan on push, which ensures that each new image pushed to the repository is scanned, and you can then retrieve the results of the image scan.

**Write it as.** `configured to **scan on push**` · `each new image pushed to the repository`

**Scope.** Amazon ECR repositories.

> "Each repository can be configured to **scan on push**. This ensures that each new image pushed to the repository is scanned. You can then retrieve the results of the image scan."
> — [What is Amazon Elastic Container Registry?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/what-is-ecr.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### ecr-scanning-basic-vs-enhanced

**Claim.** Enhanced scanning integrates Amazon ECR with Amazon Inspector for automated, continuous scanning of both operating system and programming language package vulnerabilities, while basic scanning uses the CVE database to scan operating system vulnerabilities on push or manually.

**Write it as.** `automated, continuous scanning of your repositories` · `scan for operating system vulnerabilities`

**Scope.** Amazon ECR image scanning.

> "Enhanced scanning** – Amazon ECR integrates with Amazon Inspector to provide automated, continuous scanning of your repositories. Your container images are scanned for both operating systems and programming language package vulnerabilities."
> — [Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)

> "Basic scanning** – Amazon ECR uses AWS native technology with the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) database to scan for operating system vulnerabilities."
> — [Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)

> "With basic scanning, you configure your repositories to scan on push or you can perform manual scans and Amazon ECR provides a list of scan findings."
> — [Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-scanning.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### ecr-tag-immutability-prevent-overwrite

**Claim.** You can prevent image tags from being overwritten by turning on tag immutability in an ECR repository. In the console setting for Immutable, you can also enter tag names or wildcards in the Immutable tag exclusion text box to enable tag updates for a few immutable tags.

**Write it as.** `prevent image tags from being overwritten` · `Immutable tag exclusion`

**Scope.** Amazon ECR private repositories; the exclusion box is described in the console steps (Setting image tag mutability, AWS Management Console); the overview sentence of the same page still says tag immutability affects all tags.

> "You can prevent image tags from being overwritten by turning on tag immutability in a repository."
> — [Preventing image tags from being overwritten in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-tag-mutability.html)

> "Additionally, to enable tag updates for a few immutable tags, enter tag names or use wildcards (\*) to match multiple similar tags in the **Immutable tag exclusion** text box."
> — [Preventing image tags from being overwritten in Amazon ECR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/image-tag-mutability.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

**Claim.** The security group attached to the ECR VPC endpoint must allow incoming connections on port 443 from the private subnet of the VPC.

### ecr-vpc-endpoints-fargate-need-ecr-and-s3

**Claim.** Amazon ECS tasks on Fargate using platform version 1.4.0 or later require both the Amazon ECR VPC endpoints and the Amazon S3 gateway endpoint, and tasks on Amazon EC2 instances also require both the Amazon ECR endpoints and the Amazon S3 gateway endpoint.

**Write it as.** `require both Amazon ECR VPC endpoints` · `the Amazon S3 gateway endpoint`

**Scope.** Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints; Fargate platform version 1.4.0 or later.

> "Amazon ECS tasks hosted on Fargate using platform version `1.4.0` or later require both Amazon ECR VPC endpoints and the Amazon S3 gateway endpoints."
> — [Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/vpc-endpoints.html)

> "Amazon ECS tasks hosted on Amazon EC2 instances require both Amazon ECR endpoints and the Amazon S3 gateway endpoint."
> — [Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECR/latest/userguide/vpc-endpoints.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.
